slides.title: You don't have to be the *smartest person* in the room.
slides.sub: Speaking reveals what you already know. Listening opens the door to what you don't.

slides.title: Curious, not defensive
slides.body: When we stop trying to prove we're the smartest person in the room, we start asking better questions.

slides.title: Notice the quiet wisdom
slides.body: Of people we might otherwise overlook. Humility turns a conversation from a contest into an exchange.

slides.title: Your voice still counts
slides.body: Listening doesn't make your voice less valuable. It makes your words more thoughtful.

slides.title: Discover, don't display
slides.body: Make the goal not to show what you know, but to find what you haven't yet considered.

slides.title: Speak when your words add clarity, encouragement, truth, or warning.
slides.body: "The Wisdom of Speaking Less" on the Journal at pathways2goodlife.com
